verses.zh: 那夜王睡不着觉，就吩咐人取历史来，念给他听。
verses.en: Throughout that night the king was unable to sleep,[NOTE:1] so he asked for the book containing the historical records[NOTE:2] to be brought. As the records[NOTE:3] were being read in the king’s presence,
notes: Heb “and the sleep of the king fled.” In place of the rather innocuous comment of the Hebrew text, the LXX reads here, “And the Lord removed the sleep from the king.” The Greek text thus understands the statement in a more overtly theological way than does the Hebrew text, although even in the Hebrew text there may be a hint of God’s providence at work in this matter. After all, this event is crucial to the later reversal of Haman’s plot to destroy the Jewish people, and a sympathetic reader is likely to look beyond the apparent coincidence.
Heb “the book of the remembrances of the accounts of the days”; NAB “the chronicle of notable events.”
Heb “they”; the referent (the records) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
6:1 "the king could not sleep" This not only shows the unseen hand of God (the LXX is specific), but
also the results of eating too much the night before at the banquet! This same divine action occurs in
Dan. 2:1; 6:1; and even in Gen. 31:40. There is certainly similarity between the lives of Joseph, Daniel,
and Mordecai.

▣ "the book of records, the chronicles" These would be official court records (cf. Esth. 2:23
and 10:2).

verses.zh: 正遇见书上写着说：王的太监中有两个守门的，辟探和提列，想要下手害亚哈随鲁王，末底改将这事告诉王后。
verses.en: it was found written that Mordecai had disclosed that Bigthana[NOTE:1] and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs who guarded the entrance, had plotted to assassinate[NOTE:2] King Ahasuerus.
notes: This individual is referred to as “Bigthan,” a variant spelling of the name, in Esth 2:21.
Heb “to send a hand against”; NASB “had sought to lay hands on.”
verses.commentary:
6:2-3 The role reversal is beginning. The king has become aware of Mordecai's service and lack of
reward from several years previous. It is amazing that the king was having read to him such old events!

verses.zh: 王说：「末底改行了这事，赐他甚么尊荣爵位没有？」伺候王的臣仆回答说：「没有赐他甚么。」
verses.en: The king asked, “What great honor[NOTE:1] was bestowed on Mordecai because of this?” The king’s attendants who served him responded, “Not a thing was done for him.”
notes: Heb “honor and greatness.” The expression is a hendiadys (see the note on 5:10 for an explanation of this figure).
verses.commentary:
6:3 The Anchor Bible, vol. 7B, p. 64, mentions that Mordecai's lack of reward would have reflected
badly on the king (cf. Herodotus, Hist. 3.138,140; 5.11; 8.85; 9.207; Thucydides, Peloponnesian
Wars 1.138).

verses.zh: 王说：「谁在院子里？」（那时哈曼正进王宫的外院，要求王将末底改挂在他所预备的木架上。）
verses.en: Then the king said, “Who is that in the courtyard?” Now Haman had come to the outer courtyard of the palace to suggest that the king hang Mordecai on the gallows that he had constructed for him.
verses.commentary:
6:4 "Who is in the court" Haman had apparently come early in the morning to request the impaling of
Mordecai. What irony!

▣ "hanging" See
Special Topic: Hang.

verses.zh: 臣仆说：「哈曼站在院内。」王说：「叫他进来。」
verses.en: The king’s attendants said to him, “It is Haman who is standing in the courtyard.” The king said, “Let him enter.”
verses.commentary:
6:5 Haman's early arrival shows his intense and continuing hatred of Mordecai. He is there to get
permission to kill him and hang him high!

verses.zh: 哈曼就进去。王问他说：「王所喜悦尊荣的人，当如何待他呢？」哈曼心里说：「王所喜悦尊荣的，不是我是谁呢？」
verses.en: So Haman came in, and the king said to him, “What should be done for the man whom the king wishes to honor?” Haman thought to himself,[NOTE:1] “Who is it that the king would want to honor more than me?”
notes: Heb “said in his heart” (so ASV); NASB, NRSV “said to himself.”
verses.commentary:
6:6 "'What is to be done for the man whom the king desires to honor'" The king is referring to Mordecai,
but Haman thinks it is himself!

▣ And Haman said to himself" Pride is an evil master!

verses.zh: 哈曼就回答说：「王所喜悦尊荣的，
verses.en: So Haman said to the king, “For the man whom the king wishes to honor,

verses.zh: 当将王常穿的朝服和戴冠的御马，
verses.en: let them bring royal attire which the king himself has worn and a horse on which the king himself has ridden—one bearing the royal insignia.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “a royal crown on his head.” The reference is to an official decoration or headdress for horses in royal service. See HALOT 506 s.v. כֶּתֶר; DCH 4:477 s.v. כֶּתֶר. Cf. TEV “a royal ornament”; CEV “a fancy headdress.”tc The final comment (“one on whose head the royal crown has been”) is not included in the LXX.
verses.commentary:
6:8-9 There seems to be a series of three things:

- a royal robe which had been worn by the king

- a royal horse which had been ridden by the king and on whose head was the symbol of the Persian crown

- a royal procession, led by the most notable princes, through the streets on this horse with its
bedecked rider and a great proclamation

verses.zh: 都交给王极尊贵的一个大臣，命他将衣服给王所喜悦尊荣的人穿上，使他骑上马，走遍城里的街市，在他面前宣告说：王所喜悦尊荣的人，就如此待他。」
verses.en: Then let this clothing and this horse be given to one of the king’s noble officials. Let him[NOTE:1] then clothe the man whom the king wishes to honor, and let him lead him about through the plaza of the city on the horse, calling[NOTE:2] before him, ‘So shall it be done to the man whom the king wishes to honor!’”
notes: The present translation reads with the LXX וְהִלְבִּישׁוֹ (vehilbisho, “and he will clothe him”) rather than the reading of the MT וְהִלְבִּישׁוּ (vehilbishu, “and they will clothe”). The reading of the LXX is also followed by NAB, NRSV, TEV, CEV, and NLT. Likewise, the later verbs in this verse (“cause him to ride” and “call”) are better taken as singulars rather than plurals.
Heb “and let them call” (see the previous note).
verses.commentary: 6:9 The purpose of honoring Mordecai was to encourage loyalty and service to the king!

verses.zh: 王对哈曼说：「你速速将这衣服和马，照你所说的，向坐在朝门的犹大人末底改去行。凡你所说的，一样不可缺。」
verses.en: The king then said to Haman, “Go quickly! Take the clothing and the horse, just as you have described, and do as you just indicated to Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king’s gate. Don’t neglect[NOTE:1] a single thing of all that you have said.”
notes: Heb “do not let fall”; NASB “do not fall short.”
verses.commentary:
6:10 "'Take quickly'" This represents two IMPERATIVES (BDB 554 I, KB 553 and
BDB 542, KB 534). This has the connotation of urgency. This honor had been long overdue.

▣ "the horse" The king's special horse is mentioned in Esth. 8:10.

▣ "and do so for Mordecai the Jew who is sitting at the king's gate" This is the
third IMPERATIVE (BDB 793, KB 889, Qal IMPERATIVE). How Ahasuerus
knew that Mordecai was a Jew is uncertain unless it was recorded in the chronicles which were read to
him the night before. It also acknowledges his apparent official position at the king's gate. It is
uncertain if the king remembered Haman's edict and realized its consequences toward Mordecai.

verses.zh: 于是哈曼将朝服给末底改穿上，使他骑上马，走遍城里的街市，在他面前宣告说：「王所喜悦尊荣的人，就如此待他。」
verses.en: So Haman took the clothing and the horse, and he clothed Mordecai. He led him about on the horse throughout the plaza of the city, calling before him, “So shall it be done to the man whom the king wishes to honor!”
verses.commentary: 6:11 Is there anything that would have upset Haman more than this? Note Esth. 6:12.

verses.zh: 末底改仍回到朝门，哈曼却忧忧闷闷地蒙着头，急忙回家去了，
verses.en: Then Mordecai again sat at the king’s gate, while Haman hurried away to his home, mournful and with a veil over his head.
verses.commentary:
6:12 "with his head covered" This was an Oriental symbol of dejection, humiliation, and mourning
(BDB 341, KB 339, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, cf. 2 Sam. 15:30; Ps. 44:15; Jer. 14:3-4).

verses.zh: 将所遇的一切事详细说给他的妻细利斯和他的众朋友听。他的智慧人和他的妻细利斯对他说：「你在末底改面前始而败落，他如果是犹大人，你必不能胜他，终必在他面前败落。」
verses.en: Haman then related to his wife Zeresh and to all his friends everything that had happened to him. These wise men,[NOTE:1] along with his wife Zeresh, said to him, “If indeed this Mordecai before whom you have begun to fall is Jewish,[NOTE:2] you will not prevail against him. No, you will surely fall before him!”
notes: Part of the Greek tradition and the Syriac Peshitta understand this word as “friends,” probably reading the Hebrew term רֲכָמָיו (rakhamayv, “his friends”) rather than the reading of the MT חֲכָמָיו (hakhamayv, “his wise men”). Cf. NLT “all his friends”; the two readings appear to be conflated by TEV as “those wise friends of his.”
Heb “from the seed of the Jews”; KJV, ASV similar.
verses.commentary:
6:13 "his wise men" These are the ones who cast the lots before Haman in Esth. 3:7. The Hebrew word
(BDB 314) often is used for a class of diviners (cf. Gen. 41:8; Exod. 7:11; Isa. 19:11; 44:25; Jer. 50:35; 51:57).

▣ "Zeresh his wife said to him" This is an unusual statement. It is somewhat similar to
Pilate's wife speaking to him during the trial of Jesus (cf. Matt. 27:19) . We simply do not know why
she spoke in this prophetic fashion. It is also similar to Balaam's prophecies in Numbers (cf. Num. 22-24).
The unseen hand of God is clearly manifesting itself (role reversal). One wonders why these counselors
did not tell him this before, as he was planning the destruction of the Jews and, later, Mordecai.
In all probability this is a literary device which reflects the author's theology proclaimed by the
mouth of Haman's wife. Biblical dialogue often carries the theological load!

verses.zh: 他们还与哈曼说话的时候，王的太监来催哈曼快去赴以斯帖所预备的筵席。
verses.en: While they were still speaking with him, the king’s eunuchs arrived. They quickly brought Haman to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
verses.commentary: 6:14 This set the stage for Haman's ultimate demotion and death.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ESTHER 6:1-9

1During that night the king could not sleep so he gave an order to bring the book of records, the chronicles, and they were read before the king. 2It was found written what Mordecai had reported concerning Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs who were doorkeepers, that they had sought to lay hands on King Ahasuerus. 3The king said, "What honor or dignity has been bestowed on Mordecai for this?" Then the king's servants who attended him said, "Nothing has been done for him." 4So the king said, "Who is in the court?" Now Haman had just entered the outer court of the king's palace in order to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows which he had prepared for him. 5The king's servants said to him, "Behold, Haman is standing in the court." And the king said, "Let him come in." 6So Haman came in and the king said to him, "What is to be done for the man whom the king desires to honor?" And Haman said to himself, "Whom would the king desire to honor more than me?" 7Then Haman said to the king, "For the man whom the king desires to honor, 8let them bring a royal robe which the king has worn, and the horse on which the king has ridden, and on whose head a royal crown has been placed; 9and let the robe and the horse be handed over to one of the king's most noble princes and let them array the man whom the king desires to honor and lead him on horseback through the city square, and proclaim before him, 'Thus it shall be done to the man whom the king desires to honor.'"
